ai_analysis.summary: This is a generic spontaneous application with no concrete job requirements, so fit is inferred from the candidate's stated goal (systems/low-level/hardware/Linux) matched against Alice & Bob's hardware-centric quantum computing domain. The candidate's Linux kernel driver, embedded (STM32/FPGA), and ASIC-level work at Arista are strong signals, but there is zero evidence of quantum computing, control-systems, or RF/cryogenics experience that such a hardware startup would likely value. Overall a plausible but speculative match (~48%) given the absence of a real job description.
resume_tips: Add 'quantum computing' or 'control systems' context/interest since Alice & Bob is a hardware-focused quantum startup, even if only in a cover letter.
Quantify the Arista ASIC register/DMA work with concrete metrics (e.g. number of chip variants supported, defects reduced) to strengthen the low-level hardware narrative.
Move Linux kernel driver (RFID) and embedded STM32/I2C/UART projects higher on the resume since they best match 'hardware interface, Linux' focus.
Explicitly mention 'real-time' and 'RTOS' vocabulary given the Synchronous Real-Time Systems and Rate Monotonic scheduler project, as hardware control companies often screen for this.
Surface FPGA/VHDL experience (Unicycle CPU) more prominently — quantum hardware companies frequently need FPGA-based control electronics skills.
Since no formal job requirements exist, tailor the cover letter to explicitly connect systems/driver experience to quantum control-system or FPGA-based instrumentation use cases.
